newsitem.title: ITALY: Stet head to define industrial plan by May.
newsitem.headline: Stet head to define industrial plan by May.

text.p: The managing director of Italian state telecoms holding Stet said he wants to outline an industrial plan for the telecommunications group by early May, setting out four objectives.

Tomaso Tommasi di Vignano said Stet, which is due to merge with state telecoms operator Telecom Italia before privatisation later this year, firstly wanted to defend its home market through cost cuts alongside a trend of falling prices.

He told a parliamentary committee the group's second objective was to boost its mobile phone services which would mean a reallocation of frequencies, taking some from the Tacs service to give to the GSM service.
Tommasi said however he had not yet had a reply from the government on this plan.
Next he wanted multimedia development, particularly in the realms of digital television and the Internet, as well as consolidating existing alliances.
Finally Stet wanted to expand its activities abroad.
"We need to evaluate our presence in countries which have have ongoing projects of privatisation in which the group might be able to take part," Tommasi said.
"For the moment we are particularly interested in south America and eastern Europe," he said.
He also stressed the need for Stet to find an international partner, saying: "We have to resolve the problem of our position with regard to global alliances."
